data.title: Amphotericin B
data.summary: Other antifungals · Polyene macrolide antifungal (from Streptomyces nodosus); also antileishmanial
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antifungals_

**Class:** Polyene macrolide antifungal (from Streptomyces nodosus); also antileishmanial

## Mechanism of action
- Binds ergosterol in fungal (and Leishmania) membranes → forms pores → leakage of ions → cell death (fungicidal)
- Some binding to human cholesterol → toxicity
- Lipid formulations (liposomal, lipid complex) deliver drug to tissues with much less nephrotoxicity

## Pharmacokinetics
- Not absorbed orally; IV only; long tissue half-life; poor CSF penetration but effective in cryptococcal meningitis

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Life-threatening deep fungal infections: mucormycosis (drug of choice, liposomal), cryptococcal meningitis (with flucytosine), disseminated histoplasmosis, blastomycosis, coccidioidomycosis, disseminated sporotrichosis, invasive candidiasis/aspergillosis, penicilliosis (talaromycosis)
- Leishmaniasis: visceral (kala-azar — India's programme uses single-dose liposomal amphotericin B 10 mg/kg), post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (alternative to miltefosine), mucosal and refractory cutaneous leishmaniasis

## Dose & formulations
- Conventional (deoxycholate): 0.5–1 mg/kg/day IV in 5% dextrose over 4–6 h (test dose 1 mg historically)
- Liposomal: 3–5 mg/kg/day (mucormycosis 5–10 mg/kg/day)
- Kala-azar (India): liposomal 10 mg/kg single infusion

## Adverse effects
- Infusion reactions: fever, chills, rigors, hypotension (premedicate with paracetamol, antihistamine, hydrocortisone)
- Nephrotoxicity (dose-limiting with conventional form) — saline loading helps
- Hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, renal tubular acidosis
- Normocytic anaemia (reduced erythropoietin), thrombophlebitis

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; caution with renal impairment (prefer liposomal)

## Drug interactions
- Nephrotoxic drugs (aminoglycosides, cyclosporine, vancomycin); corticosteroids and diuretics worsen hypokalaemia (digoxin toxicity)

## Monitoring
- Daily renal function, K⁺ and Mg²⁺ initially; CBC; LFT

## Pregnancy & lactation
Drug of choice for serious fungal infections in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Binds ergosterol → pores
- Liposomal form for mucormycosis and single-dose kala-azar
- Nephrotoxicity and hypokalaemia

_Sources: Khopkar ch.2 and ch.5 (antileishmanial); Wolverton 4e ch.10 and ch.12. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
